flawed_step: Step 1 (justified): by Steinitz's theorem, a 3-connected cubic planar graph is the graph of a simple 3-polytope. Step 2 (cannot be justified): the claim that such a graph always has a Hamiltonian cycle, e.g. via Tait's route of building one from the faces or from a Tait coloring. No general argument can work here, because the claim is false. Tutte's fragment argument shows that some such graphs have no Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: The Tutte graph, with 46 vertices and 69 edges. It is cubic, planar and 3-connected, but not Hamiltonian. It is built from a central vertex v joined to three copies of the Tutte fragment. Each fragment also has one edge to each of the other two fragments. Fact about the fragment: any Hamiltonian cycle of the whole graph that enters and leaves a fragment must use that fragment's edge to v. A Hamiltonian cycle passes through v using exactly two of v's three edges. So one fragment's edge to v goes unused, yet the cycle must still pass through that fragment using its other two edges. That contradicts the fact above, so no Hamiltonian cycle exists.
assessment_summary: The statement is Tait's conjecture from 1884. Tutte disproved it in 1946. The Tutte graph meets every condition in the definitions (finite, simple, 3-regular, planar, 3-connected) and has no Hamiltonian cycle, so the statement is false.
